designs.title: Byron Bay
designs.why: The Cape Byron lighthouse on the headland, with the long sweep of beach below, is exactly the view you remember from the walk up. The engraving is crisp and the name is big and readable from across a room. It looks like a souvenir I'd actually wear rather than a tourist-shop tee. The small 'Ocean People Freedom' slogans are generic filler.
designs.fix: Clip the scene to the inner circle. At about 3 o'clock it ends in a straight vertical edge with a notch where the ring steps, and up close that looks like a production mistake.

designs.title: Playa Venao
designs.why: It's clean and well drawn, and the name will mean something to the people who've been there. But nothing in the scene is specific to Venao. The palms, signpost and generic headland would work for any beach, so it relies entirely on the name. The 'Surf Explore Relax Repeat' signpost feels like a stock gift-shop line.
designs.fix: Add one thing locals would recognise, like the wide horseshoe bay with the point break or the beachfront hostel rancho, and swap the 'Relax Repeat' signs for something less clichéd.

designs.title: Ericeira
designs.why: This is the best of the set. The whitewashed village on the cliffs, the stone stairs and the board leaning on the wall really feel like Ericeira, and they break away from the palm-tree formula the others share. It reads well on both tees, and 'Small Town Big Waves' is a line I'd actually repeat.
designs.fix: Fix the straight-cut edge and broken ring segment on the right side so the badge outline is a clean circle.

designs.title: San Juan del Sur
designs.why: The Christ statue on the hill above the bay is a great, accurate detail, and 'Surf, Tacos, Sunset, Amigos' is fun. But 'Pura Vida' is Costa Rica's slogan, not Nicaragua's, and any surfer who has crossed that border would spot it straight away and feel the shirt was made by someone who's never been there.
designs.fix: Replace 'Pura Vida' with something truly Nicaraguan. 'Tuani' works, or simply 'Playa Maderas' or another nearby break.

designs.title: Haleiwa
designs.why: 'North Shore' and 'Shave Ice' are spot on, and the wave looks good. The mountain, though, reads as Diamond Head, which is in Waikiki on the other side of the island from Haleiwa. North Shore surfers will notice, and that undercuts the whole point of a local badge.
designs.fix: Swap the Diamond Head silhouette for the Waianae range or Ka'ena side as seen from Haleiwa, or for the Rainbow Bridge, Matsumoto's or a North Shore lineup.

designs.title: Puerto Escondido
designs.why: The thick, heaving barrel is the hero of the scene, and that is exactly what Zicatela is known for. 'Big Waves Wild Energy' fits the place too. The cliff-top palapa is a nice touch, and the long name still arcs neatly and readably.
designs.fix: Push the wave even bigger and hollower, close to Mexican Pipeline scale, so it's unmistakably Puerto rather than a generic peeling wave.

designs.title: Montañita
designs.why: The bamboo bar with string lights and the 'Surf Food Music Friends' signs capture Montañita's party-town feel well, and the Ñ is spelled properly. The left side gets busy, though, with the hut, signs and palms crowding together, so from a distance it reads as a dark mass.
designs.fix: Thin out the foliage around the bar so the hut and signs stand apart from it, and fix the clipped right edge of the ring.

designs.title: Tamarindo
designs.why: It's an easy sell. 'Pura Vida Siempre' is right for Costa Rica, the sunset-and-palm scene suits Tamarindo's vibe, and 'Costa Rica' sits clean along the bottom. But it's the most generic scene of the eight and could be any tropical beach.
designs.fix: Add a Tamarindo marker, such as the river-mouth break or Isla Capitán offshore, so it feels like that specific beach.
